title: Did someone already managed to do polished graphics with AI?
author: rainbooow
selftext:
Hi,

I worked for a few months already on a pokemon-like autobattler, which is shaping nicely - the worst part though is that the graphics are still very rough. I recently stumbled upon a game with a very similar concept, but [much more polished graphics](https://shared.fastly.steamstatic.com/store_item_assets/steam/apps/3669200/1afffd53c3ccedfbbce402af54e8286bd84d1882/ss_1afffd53c3ccedfbbce402af54e8286bd84d1882.1920x1080.jpg?t=1784638648). 

I don't want my game to look exactly like this one (which does copy quite a bit the Teamfight Tactics graphic chart itself), and I am not an artist myself, but I was wondering: do you think this type of quality (or close to it) is reachable with the current maturity of AI tools? What would the dev flow look like? 

What I did so far (a few months ago, maybe it is better those days) when I iterated on the graphics was: nano banana for initial art --> veo to get a animation --> extract frames and create a spritesheet. So I have kind of okay animation, but the rest (background image / map, etc.) is very barebone, and I am wondering how I should approach it: should i try to design 1 by 1 individual elements, then compose the overall background with those elements? Should I just try to have a single image with everything in it?

comments.author: Livid_Shallot5701
comments.body: the problem is not that its not reachable with ai art, the problem is that you need proper animations, be it 2d or 3d, which ai currently still sucks at.

replies.author: FailedGradAdmissions
replies.body:
2D is doable, expensive but you can already have GPT image 2 generate each animation frame and adjust it by hand.

If you mean fully automated, yeah not reachable and not anytime soon

replies.author: rainbooow
replies.body: Does it work to generate each animation frame like this? From my experience 6 months ago, doing it image by image was very bad, and the resulting animation not consistent at all. Which is why I went with image -> video -> frame extract instead. Which works relatively well.

replies.author: FailedGradAdmissions
replies.body: Works well for pixel art, you can even ask it to generate a sprite sheet, but Image 2 was released on April. So this wasn’t a thing 6 months ago, and I haven’t had success with clean non pixel art.

replies.author: MindlessAd4611
replies.body:
yeah that works great for me as well (:  
A few hours of setting up a pipeline and now a new character is as easy as prompt -> approve -> wait 15 mins -> fully playable character with animations for all movements. using gpt-image-2 via codex-cli (skip the api costs..) and [fal.ai](http://fal.ai) for Wan 2.2 ITV, so total of \~2$ per avatar. now trying to get it setup for generating "alive" maps by animating parallax bands in the same approach. so far a bit trickier to get it tight but i think will work eventually

replies.author: Livid_Shallot5701
replies.body: thats exactly what i did. i let it create an animation in godot and handdrafted it. but thats still me doing it manually. ofc the whole structure was prepared  what i felt was a godblessing. just open an animation, move some bones and be done, no rigging, no layer management, my units are even randomized from different parts like eyes, hands, weapons, etc. and i had to code nothing of that. im so happy

replies.author: rainbooow
replies.body: I am trying to do something much simpler though, which is 2D animations. So the end artifact is basically a spritesheet with all the frames for a given animation. Do you think that going through a game engine / blender is needed to reach high quality? I know very little in term of animation (or even game development, I am a standard software engineer), do you typically rig and do layer management even for 2D animation?

replies.author: Livid_Shallot5701
replies.body:
i only do 3d animation and 2d-rigging/parts animation (spine, godot) so i do not realy know, what the current standard is, but the REASON i never toughed it in 2d (even before ai i was working already as 2d, 2.5d and 3d artist) is, that i hate drawing a ton of frames and when i dislike the animation i have like 100 drawing going to shit. i tried that a few times but i nearly kill people its that frustrating for me.

so to try to answer your post: sounds possible, but i would not trust for the life of me the ai to draw actual good and ***consistent*** animation frames. i **Hope** you prove me wrong and it looks amazing, then plz message me i wanna see it, but having the ai make animatrions frame by frame sounds to me like currently it cannot work. ( im not saying it wont work in 3 years, we all know how fast they get better).

replies.author: rainbooow
replies.body: I mean, its not doing it frame by frame, its image -> video -> frame. I managed to do this already 5 months ago, and the animation was good. But the problem was that the image, and especially video model (nano banana / veo) were very bad at following instructions: a random boob (yes...) could happen on a pokemon-like monster during the 8 seconds veo video, for no fuckin reason, or it was systematically creating base shadow for it, even though I tried 20 ways of prompting it to not do it.

replies.author: Cubey42
replies.body: Actually i think fable is pretty impressive in the animation department but it also depends on how much patience you have. I have a game in hoping to make a post this week about it, but it has animated buildings and I think it will surprise people just how complex things can be done without much expertise.

comments.author: OldManActual

comments.author: ThisGuyCrohns
comments.body:
You can’t. It won’t work. You can have it create concept art, and some sprites. But not cohesive and not great because pixels. It just can’t do art. I have tried. It can’t get lighting correctly, shading etc. yes you can have it generate an image, but that’s not quality polished art.

I have tried. I even went down to 8-bit pixels to see how well it could do. It is horrible at create art without generating images through image gen.

replies.author: rainbooow
replies.body: Right, this is another requirement I forgot to add in my post: art obviously needs to be consistent. So I don't know if giving him a bank of assets currently in the game and asking the AI to adhere to them would work, but you are telling me that it does not, which is a pity :/.

replies.author: ThisGuyCrohns
replies.body: I have tried. And I mean I did everything I could. Polished in game assets can’t be image gen and slices. That would look really bad. It’s just not there yet on visually understanding quality. My attempts tried a week straight to create in game sprite assets at high quality, spent even 6 hour long sessions trying over and over, each time quality is just not there. No prompting can solve that

comments.author: NullzeroJP
comments.body:
At the moment, I think you can get good code out of AI. That should be the main focus of your AI workflows. Focus on a fun game that feels good to play. The artwork, either ai generated or store bought or custom ordered... can come later.

So, AI is good a code... but when it comes to art assets, they are not quite there yet. Concept art, single one-off characters or portraits, definitely possible. From my understanding anime-style generations are quite good. But full sprite animations with effects, proper alignment and proper animation frames... it's going to be a battle. I even had trouble generating simple 9-slice UI assets for Unity. It can generate the assets, but they are often grainy, and generate with JPEG compression artifacts... its hilarious. Imagine generating sprites with compression artifacts before compression even takes place! Haha... what a joke. And when I used nano banana, I would ask for transparent backgrounds... and it would create opaque backgrounds with checkered patterns on them... basically a "fake" transparent background... they may have fixed that in the last 3 or 4 months, I'm not sure... but it was just stupid the hoops I had to jump through to get working assets.

That said... things are changing fast. I haven't tried it yet, but I bet you could get good sprite animations out of one of the big video generator sites. I forgot their names... Seadance? Kling? Maybe you could use one of them to create a video with the animations you want for a character. The output would be a full 4-8 second video. Then you would clip out the individual frames (probably via script of some kind). The crops would probably be grainy due to compression, but you could run a filter on them easily enough. But I havnt tried it, so I cant say whether it works or not.

replies.author: rainbooow
replies.body:
Dont tell me about transparent background, I run into the same but work around with a custom processing pipeline doing that kind of things (removing background, doing several iteration of the same prompt, etc.).

Problem is, a big part of developing a game is the art part. Sure, you can get some games being carried purely by their gameplay, but in most cases, good visual experience is part of the package and does contribute to the fun.

replies.author: NullzeroJP
replies.body:
Yes, I ended up doing a similar workflow to remove transparency. I eventually just asked it to generate pure black backgrounds and did crops, and then an AI filter to remove the fake jpeg compression artifacts. We are close. You can tell the technology is there, its just not specialized for game dev yet.

As for the movie thing, thats cool to hear. 5 months ago feels like 5 years though, when talking AI development. I bet its gotten much better since then. I really want to try it, but just haven't had time yet.

comments.author: Late-Oven-9575

comments.author: Bratchan
comments.body:
Getting a base understanding WITHOUT AI.. will help you understand how to use AI to aid you. 

I also have found. Havign AI make you small portions of game engine for your game helps as well. So you have more control than letting AI handle it all for you as well. it will give you more control.  And havign taht base understanding og animale 2d or 3d will aid you more when you tell AI what you need it to build so you have more control.

replies.author: throwaway12222018
replies.body:
I think being able to explicitly articulate your ideas and every detail, paired with systems thinking is enough to get good output.

I don't have any background in game development, rendering pipelines, or asset creation, but I have a background in math and non-game programming, which is basically enough to iterate with AI and achieve good results.
